title: Ban on Ex-offenders from Donating Blood within One Year of Release from Prison
what_it_is: Ban on Ex-offenders from Donating Blood within One Year of Release from Prison

sections.label: HSA one-year blood deferral
sections.summary: HSA adopted a one-year deferral period aligned with Australia, Canada and the United States to let screening tests detect blood-borne infections.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: HSA has adopted a one-year deferral period, aligned with the practices of other countries such as Australia, Canada and the United States of America.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It ensures that the window period after these donors become infected has passed, enabling the screening tests to detect blood-borne infections if any, as patient safety is utmost important and cannot be compromised.

sections.label: Inmate blood donation deferral
sections.summary: Inmates face a 12-month deferral as HIV prevalence is 1.1% among inmates versus 0.2% in the general population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Although there are no reported instances of inmates contracting blood-borne or infectious diseases while in Singapore's prison – and this is something that we are very proud of as compared to many of the other prisons that Mr Louis Ng has alluded to – we still need to err on the side of caution as inmates may have contracted the infectious diseases before their admission to prison.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: If I can just quote some statistics: for HIV, for the general population between the age 15 and 45 in Singapore, the HIV prevalence is 0.2% but it is 1.1% amongst inmates or ex-inmates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This is a fact that they are of a higher risk profile.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I also thank the ex-inmate who came forward to donate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I think for genuine donors, they can still continue to come forward to donate their blood after that 12-month deferral period.

sections.label: Mental illness blood donation
sections.summary: Patients with mental illness may donate blood if certification from their psychiatrist or doctor shows they can make their own decisions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: There is a wide spectrum of mental illnesses – from very mild mental conditions to very severe conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: So, as long as the patient with mental illness is able to prove from maybe some form of certification from their psychiatrist or doctor that they able to make decisions on their own, then, we will be able to accept them as blood donors.

sections.label: Genuine donors after deferral
sections.summary: Genuine donors are still welcomed to donate blood after the 12-month deferral period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Like I have mentioned, for genuine donors, they are still welcomed to donate after the 12-month deferral period.
